questions.q: What is the correct order for configuring a working REST Message?
options: Add Functions first, then configure the parent Endpoint, then test
Configure the parent Endpoint and Authentication Profile, add Functions for real operations, then test each Function
Test a Function before it has been created
Order doesn't matter as long as everything is filled in eventually
questions.explain: The base Endpoint and credential live on the parent and every Function's path builds on them, so configuring the parent first, then adding and testing Functions, catches mistakes early.

questions.q:
Given this Function configuration:

Function: createCustomer
  HTTP Method: POST
  Endpoint: /customers
  HTTP Header: Content-Type = application/json
  Content: {"email":"${email}","name":"${name}"}

Why does this Function need a Content field but the GET-based getCustomerByEmail Function from the same lesson does not?
options: POST requests never need a Content field either
A GET can carry a Content body too, it's just optional for both
POST sends data to create a resource, so it needs a request body template; GET only needs a query-string placeholder in its path
Content is required on every Function regardless of HTTP method
questions.explain: A GET to look up data typically needs no body, just a path/query placeholder; a POST that creates a resource needs a body template with its own placeholders, plus a Content-Type header.

questions.q: What does the Test capability on a REST Message Function actually do?
options: It simulates a response locally without contacting the external system
It only validates that the JSON syntax in the Content field is well-formed
It sends a real, live HTTP request to the configured Endpoint using the configured Authentication Profile, and returns the real status code and body
It permanently deletes the Function record if the test fails
questions.explain: Test is a genuine outbound call from inside the record, not a simulation — exactly what lets you verify configuration before any script exists.

questions.q: You run Test on a Function and get back HTTP status 401. What does that most likely indicate?
options: The external system is completely down
The Authentication Profile is wrong or stale
The relative path on the Function is misspelled
The request body contains invalid JSON
questions.explain: 401 is an authentication failure — the credential in the Authentication Profile is the first thing to check, distinct from a 404 (bad path) or 500 (server-side error).

questions.q: Why does testing a Function from the record, before writing any script, actually save time later?
options: It doesn't — testing from the record provides no real benefit over testing from script
It isolates configuration problems (wrong path, stale credential, missing header) from script-logic problems, so a later script failure can be assumed to be script-side
It removes the need for an Authentication Profile entirely
It automatically writes the Script Include code for you
questions.explain: A clean 200 from Test confirms the REST Message configuration is correct; any failure encountered later when calling it from script is then known to be a script-side issue, not a configuration one.
